settings.order: shuffled per rep, all measurements interleaved

meter_tiers.name: perf_counters
meter_tiers.evidence: no CPU PMU in sys/bus/event_source/devices; paranoid=2

meter_tiers.name: cachegrind
meter_tiers.evidence: valgrind-3.22.0 ran cachegrind with cache simulation on /bin/true

timer.label: measured
timer.meaning: min_step_ns is the smallest gap two reads can show (bounded by read cost), so timed windows should be >> it; getres_ns_reported is the kernel's claim

ridge_flops_per_byte_f64.label: derived
ridge_flops_per_byte_f64.meaning: arithmetic intensity above which all-core f64 work is compute-bound (roofline)

far_over_near_latency.label: derived
far_over_near_latency.meaning: cost of a load from the farthest level found vs the nearest

memory_levels_method: BIC piecewise-constant fit of log(median latency), weights 1/SE_median^2 (bootstrap); neighbours merged unless apart by more than t(df=reps-1, 2-sided 5% Bonferroni over n-1 breakpoints) combined SE; a level must span >= 2x size with fitted rise within t(df, 2-sided 5%) SE; adjacent levels that a single line fits as well as a step joined linearly across the points between (BIC) are demoted to transition; capacity bracket starts at the last size where no rep already reached the next level
caveats: Tier 2 only unless a tier-1 meter is listed as available: these are times, not energy.
Latency includes TLB effects at large sizes; huge pages were requested (madvise) and THP mode is recorded.
In a VM, reported caches and core counts are the hypervisor's claim; measured levels may differ.
memory_levels are a fit to the measured curve (derived), not direct measurements; capacities are brackets.
Noise is within this run on this machine; it says nothing about other runs or other hosts.
